screens.notes: The only approved screen that uses AG Grid. Settlement order: run checks → reauthorize any hold past its honor period → capture winners with final_capture → void everyone else who holds an authorization (including guests with no bids) → issue receipts. Settlement stays a manual organizer action, as designed. Undrawn states the flow needs: live (before close: would-charge figures, CTA disabled, demo close control), charging (per-row progress), charged (summary; receipts issued), a failed or pending row with retry, a failing check. In a judge's private demo only real paddles hold PayPal authorizations; simulated guests must be settled in simulation and labeled honestly (one line, needs approval), since the rail says '$43,950 held with PayPal'.

Invariant checked in placeBid, setMaxBid, confirmPlan and editPlan: Σ over the paddle's lots of commitment ≤ active hold amount, where commitment = the active limit's max if one exists, else the current high bid if leading, else the won amount if closed and won, else 0. Display 'left' = hold − high bids − won amounts (10 labels the reserved part as Glim's room). Bids after closes_at are refused whether or not the worker has closed the lot.

Seed sources (numbers already reconcile across 05–14): the 24-lot table (category, title, donor, estimated value, starting bid, min raise), the ledger names and amounts, the projector activity and Jamie's story come from the approved mockups 10–14; the seed now holds them in src/server/demo/ (template.ts, roster.ts, story.ts).
golden_path: 1. The judge opens the hosted site (Fairhold home, undrawn) and clicks 'Start a demo gala'. The server clones the Riverside Shelter Gala template into a private event: 24 seeded lots with estimated values; about 85 simulated guests with simulated holds and scripted bidding; lot closes compressed to about 15 minutes (8 staggered, the rest at the event close). The browser session gets a guest paddle (the judge types a first name) and organizer rights for this event only.

2. 09 Set your bidding power ('Not set' in the nav). The judge picks $500 and clicks 'Hold $500 with PayPal'. The server creates an Orders v2 order with intent AUTHORIZE; the PayPal sandbox window opens; the judge logs in with the sandbox buyer account listed in the testing instructions and approves; the return page calls /authorize; the authorization id and expiration are stored; the window closes and the nav reads '$500 / $500'.

3. 08 Lots: tiles update live as simulated guests bid. The judge opens Lot 07 (05), keeps the next minimum and clicks 'Place bid'. The server checks lot open, minimum raise and Σ commitments ≤ $500; the card shows 'You're winning' and the nav shows what is left. No PayPal call is made per bid.
4. A scripted guest outbids the judge on a second lot; 08 shows 'You're outbid' with 'Bid again'. Optional: a bid larger than the remaining bidding power is refused with the reason (code enforces).

5. 07: the judge clicks the orb or 'Let Glim bid for me' and writes a budget and wishes (e.g. '$500. I really want the chef's dinner. Spa only under $120.'). Claude returns a plan; code validates it (each limit ≥ next minimum, total ≤ hold) and shows the plan card. The judge clicks 'Start bidding'.

6. Glim acts inside the plan: an opening bid on Spa Day; when a scripted guest bids on Chef's Table, the engine raises to the limit and Glim posts 'Someone bid $360. I raised to $380, your limit for this lot.' Asking Glim to bid past the hold gets a refusal and an offer to raise bidding power.
7. 10 My paddle: hold vs winning bids, Glim's room, each lot with Glim's limit, the activity log, Pause and Edit plan; a nudge appears when a plan lot nears its close at the limit.

8. Organizer: the judge switches to the organizer view (undrawn switch). 12 shows the live ledger (AG Grid) with the judge's row among simulated guests; 14 Projector in another tab shows the room screen updating live.

9. Close or fast-forward: lots close on their own compressed schedule, or the demo-only controls 'Close next lot' and 'Close bidding now' set close times to now. The worker closes lots, fixes winners and marks the event closed; bids after close are refused regardless of worker timing.
10. 12 switches to 'Bidding closed · Ready to charge' and runs the checks (winners within holds, Glim bids within limits, a GET on each real authorization). The judge clicks 'Charge N winners'.

11. The worker settles: the judge's authorization is captured for the won total with final_capture: true (the rest is released), or voided if the judge won nothing; simulated guests settle in simulation; rows update live; receipts are issued; PayPal webhooks (PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED / PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.VOIDED) reconcile.

12. 11 Receipt in the guest view: amount paid with PayPal and amount released, the PayPal transaction ID (the real sandbox capture id), per-lot estimated value and tax-deductible line, Glim's recap, 'Download receipt' (PDF). The judge can confirm the capture and the released hold in the sandbox buyer account.

13. Seeing both PayPal outcomes in one run: open a private window as a second guest, hold an amount, bid low and lose; that paddle's authorization is voided at settlement. 'Raise bidding power' also produces a real void (the old hold is released once the new one is approved).

14. Reset: 'Reset demo' (or 'Start a new demo') voids any live sandbox authorizations of that demo and re-seeds; abandoned demos are voided and deleted automatically after a few hours. Holds created before submission cannot last until Dec 15 (29-day validity), so every judge creates fresh holds.
15. Video: the same path on a showcase event with 2–3 real sandbox buyers (one loses, so the void is real) plus simulated guests, using fast-forward to stay under 3 minutes.
unbuilt_screens_needed: MUST · Fairhold home + join: one page with 'Start a demo gala' (creates the private demo event) and a first-name field that assigns a paddle; says where the sandbox buyer login is; carries the Fairhold name. Why: the flow needs an entry point and a guest identity without passwords or account creation.

MUST · PayPal popup return/cancel pages: 'Approving your hold…', 'Approved, you can close this window', 'Canceled', and the full-page redirect used when the popup is blocked. Why: the hold approval round trip needs a landing page.

MUST · Role switch and demo controls: a menu on the paddle/organizer pill to switch Guest view ↔ Organizer view (demo events only), plus demo-only 'Close next lot', 'Close bidding now' and 'Reset demo'. Why: judges must reach 12 and close the event without waiting.

MUST · Control room states not drawn: live (before close), charging, charged, a failed row or failed check, and one honest line that simulated guests settle without PayPal. Why: 12 is drawn only at 'Ready to charge'.

MUST · Receipt states not drawn: won nothing (authorization voided, never charged) and closed-not-yet-charged. Why: a judge who loses, or looks before the organizer charges, would otherwise land on an undesigned page.

MUST · One 'states sheet' image for variants built from approved parts: 05 outbid / no bid / not set / not enough bidding power / Max… entry / closed; 08 not-set band and closed tiles; 07 first open / thinking / error / plan edit / paused / off duty; 09 Other… / waiting / canceled / raise mode; 10 empty / paused; 13 ready / new lot; 14 before open / after close; plus about 10 new lot drawings. Why: the user approves every visible change, and one sheet keeps it to one round.

SHOULD · Organizer Lots index (/organizer/lots) as an AG Grid based on 13b's grid without its rail: inline estimated-value editing, Ready / Needs a value chips, search, pager; a row opens 13. Why: the organizer 'Lots' link needs a destination, and it adds a second, editable AG Grid for the sponsor prize (13 itself has none).

SHOULD · 'How it works' page for the guest nav, reusing 09's 'How the hold works' panel and Glim's rule line; or approve removing the link. Why: a dead nav link hurts the 'complete product experience' criterion.

SHOULD · Phone layout of the guest pages (single column of 08, 05, 09, 10, 11, with the chat as a bottom sheet). Why: the projector tells the room to bid from a phone and the brief says phones or laptops, but every approved guest screen is desktop.
COULD · Bidders page for the organizer nav: an AG Grid of paddles with PayPal hold status (authorized, honor period, expires, reauthorized); or approve removing the link.

CUT · Organizer event setup, password sign-up/sign-in, multi-event admin, and a Glim chat on organizer pages: demo events are cloned from the seeded template, and on organizer pages the orb only shows its bubble.
